passages.text: After saying these things, he sent the advance party to Antioch in Syria, telling them to wait there the following day. After they had gone, Peter drove away diseases, afflictions, and demons from large crowds who had been persuaded, baptized them in the nearby springs in the sea, and broke the Eucharist. He appointed Maron, who had received him and was by now mature, as overseer, designated twelve elders, appointed attendants, and organized arrangements for widows. He discussed the order that served the common or beneficial interest of the assembly and advised them to obey Maron the overseer. Since three months had now been completed, he took leave of those in Tripolis in Phoenicia and set out on the road to Antioch in Syria, with everyone accompanying us on our way with the appropriate honor.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to wait there the following day
lexical_decisions.rationale: The following is understood with the ordinary elliptical day; no exact date is supplied.
The source combines breaking with Eucharist/thanksgiving, implicitly its bread. The breaking action is retained rather than merely offered thanks.
Translates the office’s sense; bishop is the conventional title alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ διακόνους δείξας καὶ χηρικὰ συστησάμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: appointed attendants, and organized arrangements for widows
lexical_decisions.rationale: διάκονοι can be attendants or deacons. χηρικά means matters/institutions for widows, not an invented beneficiary list.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπέρ τε τοῦ κοινοῦ ἢ συμφέροντος τῆς ἐκκλησίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: that served the common or beneficial interest of the assembly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the supplied or instead of silently changing it to and; the precise relation between common and beneficial remains loose.
